transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (SignalWave - Head of Procurement), Evan Liu (SignalWave - Security Lead), Marco Serrano (SignalWave - SRE Manager), Lena Torres (SignalWave - Legal Counsel)

Auto-summary (auto): Customer is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference to meet latency SLAs and enterprise security controls. Legal has a few DPA/MSA questions and procurement needs pricing bands for committed capacity. Technical team requested a short benchmark and clarification on KMS/privileged onboarding.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side - i'm maya, AE on this account, and daniel is our se. this is the procurement/legal gate, we want to make sure the contract artifacts and the tech preflight are squared away before you go to your internal sourcing committee.
[00:28] Priya Rao: Thanks Maya. yes, priority for us is to understand pricing at different commit levels, any data residency obligations, and the exact SLA language. also want the timeline for pilot to be clear.
[00:45] Daniel Park: Great. From the SE perspective i'll cover the benchmark plan and the private/VPC options, also how KMS/HSM integrations look. quick note — i may say "Redwood Dedicaed" by accident, sorry for that — i mean "Dedicated".
[01:10] Evan Liu: Cool. On security side we need to see SOC2 report, key management details, and confirm that logs/audit trails are available and can be exported to our SIEM. Also, is there any privileged onboarding for platform admins?
[01:35] Maya Chen: Yep. We will share SOC2 and the compliance pack. privileged access — we support RBAC + SSO (SAML) and can integrate customer-managed KMS for keying on Private deployments. For Hosted, we offer bring-your-own-key with our KMS partners, but we'll call that out in the DPA.
[02:05] Marco Serrano: Quick question — for the Dedicated option, how isolated is the GPU pool? e.g., can we guarantee physical separation or is it tenant-shared with compute isolation?
[02:28] Daniel Park: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool logically isolated; we can also discuss single-tenant physical hosts for higher tiers but that tends to be an enterprise add-on. i'll include the isolation matrix in the docs.
[02:55] Priya Rao: On pricing: we need three tiers — evaluation pilot (small), committed monthly throughput, and enterprise reserved. we also need egress and KMS fees called out. any flexibility on contract length vs discount?
[03:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we have flexible commit bands — monthly and annual. discounts increase with longer commit and higher GPU hours. we'll send a tailored pricing matrix. note there can be egress and keying fees depending on KMS provider.
[03:45] Evan Liu: About the DPA: we have a couple of mandatory clauses around data residency and breach notification timelines. Also, we prefer customer-managed keys where possible — we won't accept vendor-managed for certain datasets.
[04:10] Lena Torres: i'll jump in — on the MSA we have typical indemnities, but the DPA has more questions. specifically, do you offer an auditable key wrap mechanism and can you commit to not accessing plaintext in the Private deployment?
[04:35] Daniel Park: For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we can commit to customer controlled keys and limited access controls — operational access is scoped and audited. We can include language that operational engineers cannot access unencrypted payloads without a formal process. i'll flag precise wording for legal to review.
[04:58] Priya Rao: Good. Also timeline — procurement committee meets next Thursday, 2025-08-22. We need to receive pricing + redlines before then to get an internal decision.
[05:18] Maya Chen: Understood — target to deliver pricing + initial MSA/DPA for your review by 2025-08-20. Is that workable?
[05:28] Priya Rao: yes that helps.
[05:35] [short crosstalk] Marco Serrano: on the technical preflight, i'll need the default batch sizes, expected token costs, and the KV cache behavior — we run heavy prefix reuse so caching behavior impacts cost.
[05:58] Daniel Park: Absolutely. The runtime supports prefix/KV caching and automatic batching. i'll detail how cache hits are measured and show token-level cost estimates. note that caching behavior depends on model selection and sequence length distribution.
[06:25] Evan Liu: About encryption in transit, do you support mutual TLS and client certs for the Private control plane? we prefer mutual auth.
[06:40] Daniel Park: Yes, mutual TLS is supported for Private. For Hosted we offer customer-controlled TLS termination via our edge partners or dedicated peering; we'll map options in the security appendix.
[06:58] Priya Rao: A procurement-level question — do you have a standard escrow or data escrow offer? Some of our stakeholders want an escrow mechanism for model weights or the service if business continuity is impacted.
[07:20] Maya Chen: We do offer escrow options for enterprise on multi-year contracts. i'll surface the escrow playbook and options for your review.
[07:38] Lena Torres: Great, please include specifics. Also, any sub processors need to be listed in the DPA.
[07:48] Maya Chen: We'll include subprocessor list in the compliance pack; some partners change quarterly but we'll mark the current set and a notification cadence.
[08:05] Marco Serrano: For the benchmark — what does Redwood need from us? we can provide a synthetic workload and a sample prompt set.
[08:18] Daniel Park: Ideal: provide representative sequences (p95 length), concurrency targets (100 qps example we discussed), and any prompt engineering that affects output. We'll run a 2-hour smoke with Dedicated instance and share perf + tail latency numbers.
[08:40] Priya Rao: If the benchmark looks good, procurement may greenlight a short pilot procurement path. But finance will still need the committed pricing matrix.
[08:55] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize sending the matrix. Daniel, can you commit to a runbook and a short write-up on expected per-token economics for their workload?
[09:08] Daniel Park: Yes — runbook + cost per thousand tokens for a sample model family, plus quantization/throughput notes. i'll include notes on Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/cache/quantization).
[09:30] Evan Liu: One more security detail — for audit logs, we need event-level retention for 13 months and a way to forward logs to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[09:45] Maya Chen: Yes, log forwarding to customer SIEM is supported and retention can be configured; longer retention and export are in the enterprise package. we'll call that out.
[10:00] [pause] Priya Rao: from legal — i will likely annotate the DPA for residency and incident SLOs. what is your standard breach notification window?
[10:18] Maya Chen: Standard is 72 hours for incidents; we can discuss tighter windows for critical data sets and will note availability in the SLA section.
[10:30] Lena Torres: 72 hours is ok as a baseline. also curious re: subcontractor audit rights. we need to ensure our auditors can validate controls.
[10:45] Daniel Park: We typically provide SOC2 reports and can arrange a controls questionnaire or a rights-to-audit clause with limited scope. i'll capture that in the compliance appendix.
[11:05] Marco Serrano: A practical question — whats the fallback behavior if Dedicated cluster is saturated? do requests failover to hosted models with different latency/cost?
[11:20] Daniel Park: We support smart routing and can failover to compatible model variants or regions. That said, failovers are policy-controlled — we can avoid routing to Hosted if that violates your data residency rules. i'll show routing policy examples.
[11:45] Priya Rao: ok good. for procurement acceptance we also need proof points — customer references, SLAs met historically, maybe a short exec summary of uptime.
[12:00] Maya Chen: We'll include uptimes, our SLA definitions, reference list, and a short one-pager on past enterprise uptime and an example incident response timeline.
[12:18] Evan Liu: On KMS again — if we bring our own KMS, what is the integration model? do you support envelope encryption and key wrapping?
[12:33] Daniel Park: Yep, envelope encryption and key wrap flows are supported. For Private deployments the master key stays in your KMS and only wrapped keys are stored. we'll document the flow and the minimal changes required.
[12:52] Priya Rao: moving to specific redlines — we may ask for a cap on indemnity and clarify SLA credits. we usually push for simpler SLA credit formulas.
[13:10] Lena Torres: Also thinking about export controls and restricted data classes. we'll flag any export-control language required.
[13:22] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll mark the parts of the MSA that speak to indemnity and SLA credits so you can propose preferred language.
[13:35] Marco Serrano: Another technical note — do you provide client libraries for orchestration or is it all REST? we use a small in-house orchestrator and want a stable SDK.
[13:50] Daniel Park: We provide SDKs (python/node) and a stable API with versioning. For Private deployments we can also bundle a deployable shim if you want local SDK hosting.
[14:05] Priya Rao: If possible, include an estimated onboarding timeline and a minimal artifact checklist for procurement so we can present to the committee.
[14:20] Maya Chen: We'll send an onboarding checklist (MSA/DPA, SOC2, pricing, pilot plan, benchmark results). Target to deliver by 2025-08-20 so you can review before 2025-08-22 meeting.
[14:35] [brief pause]
[14:45] Evan Liu: One risk item: third-party subprocessors. we need to know any cloud providers or telemetry processors used.
[14:58] Daniel Park: We'll enumerate subprocessors and show the minimal telemetry retained.
[15:10] Priya Rao: ok, procedurally — procurement needs the signed MSA and a PO for pilot spend? or can we do trial credits?
[15:25] Maya Chen: For pilots we can do a short-term PO or trial credits depending on the size. small pilots often start with credits then convert to a PO for committed capacity. we'll surface options in the pricing doc.
[15:40] Marco Serrano: Also, any data egress cost estimates for cross-region requests? we have services in eu-west and us-east.
[15:55] Daniel Park: We'll provide egress estimates by region and a sample monthly bill simulation for expected throughput.
[16:10] Lena Torres: Any records retention policy for customer content? that should be in the DPA.
[16:22] Maya Chen: Yes, retention is configurable; default is 30 days for transient content unless you request otherwise. we'll include retention controls in the DPA.
[16:38] [longer discussion omitted in transcript for brevity, key points recorded] ...
[28:00] Maya Chen: To recap: Redwood will send pricing + MSA/DPA redline draft by 2025-08-20; SE will run benchmark and share runbook/results by 2025-08-22; customer will return legal redlines by 2025-08-26; procurement will confirm committee date.
[28:25] Priya Rao: Yup. One more ask — can you include a short appendix that maps our security requirements to your controls? a 2-page mapping would help the committee.
[28:40] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll prepare a controls mapping table (NIST-ish) and attach SOC2 artifacts.
[29:00] Marco Serrano: For the benchmark, can you scope a 2-hour smoke with 10k tokens/sec? that may be high, maybe 100 qps at p95 length 512. we'll send exact numbers.
[29:18] Daniel Park: 100 qps with p95 512 sounds fine as a representative workload. we'll size accordingly.
[29:30] Priya Rao: Great. Anything else from the legal side?
[29:35] Lena Torres: Not now, we'll do annotations.
[29:40] Evan Liu: No further security items.
[29:43] Maya Chen: Thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff after procurement sign-off.
[29:52] Priya Rao: Thanks everyone.
[29:56] [call ends]

Notes: Some timestamps above are approximate; the automated transcription had a few speaker attribution errors early on ("Redwood Dedicaed" misread). References shared: pricing-template.xlsx (link), compliance-pack.zip (link), benchmark-runbook.md (link).
